answer: Every epoch the network publishes a fresh beacon value, and each identity must bind its next job to it: hash one completed task with the beacon and let three random peers re-run a slice of it. Picture the beacon as a lighthouse and each proof as a crystal set on a knoll, visible to anyone passing by. A fake cannot copy a proof, because the beacon changes each epoch and peers re-run the real work, not a summary. Keeping 100 fakes alive costs 100 job slices per epoch, about 20 hours of compute, plus a 400-token bond per identity that any one peer can slash on a mismatch.
